problems: The blind guess (a stick figure with head, raised arm and two legs) does not match the intended subject, the Wick Shears. The drawing does not read as shears to a viewer, so the figure is not identifiable from its silhouette.

The stars are on the intended parts: handles at the top (66249 at about (260,148), 64238 at about (371,240)), rivet at the centre (65474 at about (302,341)), blade tips at the bottom (65639 at about (292,428), 64407 at about (359,433)). The mapping is correct.
The figure is the right way up, with handles at the top and blade tips at the bottom.

It is not a real silhouette. It is made of thin gold line segments and small blue ring outlines, so it reads as a wireframe or X/V diagram rather than a solid shape. The loops are tiny rings, not recognisable bow-handle loops, and the blades are hairline strokes.

Labels collide with the drawing: 'rivet where the two blades c...' runs over the blade lines and the star field, 'left blade tip' sits on the left blade, and the ring-handle labels are truncated ('centre of' with the rest cut off).
Background stars are scattered without forming any part of the shears, which adds noise rather than defining the outline.
output.advice: Redraw so the shears read as a solid silhouette. Fill or thicken the two blades as tapered shapes running from the rivet (65474, about (302,341)) out to the tips (65639 about (292,428); 64407 about (359,433)). Make each ring handle a visible loop around its star (66249 about (260,148); 64238 about (371,240)), with a closed, filled bow shape rather than a thin ring. Keep the blades crossing at the rivet so the X pivot is clear. Keep the handles above and the tips below. Move labels outside the figure with leader lines, so they do not sit on blades or stars, and shorten them so none are truncated (e.g. 'left ring handle', 'rivet', 'left blade tip', 'right blade tip'). Thin or remove background stars near the figure so the outline stands out. The gold lines should trace the silhouette's edges, not sit on top of an open wireframe.
